children: Our Bureau New Delhi: Used-car retailer Spinny has made a confidential filing with the Securities and Exchange Board of India for its initial public offering (IPO), according to people aware of the matter. The company is targeting a total issue size of 3,000-3,500 crore, almost equally split between primary capital raise and an offer for sale by existing investors.

The Gurugram-based company, which runs an online platform for used-car sales and competes with the likes of SoftBank-backed Cars24, is on an expansion mode and may utilise the fresh capital to expand its footprint in the country, said one of the persons, who did not wish to be identified. Spinny currently sells cars in 30 cities across India and has a supplier network in 100 cities, with plans to add 10 more cities in the near term, according to the person.

In February, the company closed a $160-170 million funding round led by US-based investors Fidelity and Accel Leaders Fund. The transaction included $90 million of primary capital, with the remaining being sold by early investors Blume Ventures and Fundamentum.

title: Used-car Retailer Spinny Files for Rs 3k-crore Listing
